purpose: Alemtuzumab is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), particularly when other MS medicines have not worked well enough. It is also sometimes used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). It helps reduce the number of MS relapses and can slow down disability progression.
how_it_works: Your immune system has special cells called B and T lymphocytes that, in MS, mistakenly attack your nervous system. Alemtuzumab is a targeted protein (antibody) that attaches to a marker called CD52 found on those harmful immune cells and destroys them. After these cells are cleared out, your immune system gradually rebuilds itself in a way that is less likely to attack your brain and spinal cord.
common_side_effects: Rash, headache, fever, chills, nausea, tiredness, flushing, and a fast or irregular heartbeat during or shortly after the infusion. You may also notice more frequent infections such as colds or urinary tract infections, as well as low blood counts.
warnings: This is a powerful medicine with serious risks. It can cause life-threatening autoimmune problems where your immune system attacks your own organs, including your kidneys, liver, or blood cells — sometimes years after treatment. There is also a higher risk of serious infections, thyroid problems, and certain cancers including blood cancers and melanoma. Because of these risks, it is only available through a special restricted program and requires regular blood and urine monitoring for at least 4 years after your last dose. Tell your doctor immediately if you notice unusual bruising, blood in urine, shortness of breath, or any new or worsening symptoms.
typical_dosing: For MS, alemtuzumab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion in two separate treatment courses. The first course is 12 mg per day infused into a vein over about 4 hours, once daily for 5 consecutive days. The second course is given 12 months later for 3 consecutive days. Additional courses may be considered if needed. It is always given in a medical setting with close monitoring.
